verdict: The spec does not meet this lens's definition of success: its build is one maintainer wide, because the no-stack rule, the manual merge and an approval line on about two tasks in three turn every dependency edge into a maintainer sitting, and its shared registries (one error table with unallocated ids, one dispatcher, one lessons file, contiguous ADR numbers, five-writer generated tables) make concurrent tasks overlap by construction.

findings.defect: The no-stack rule plus the working agreement that every merge waits for the maintainer makes the calendar critical path equal to the task graph's depth in maintainer sittings, and the only decision that could change it is deferred until tools/ci dora lands with ci-release.
findings.scenario: Twelve agents finish twelve branches in a day; the trunk advances one chain link per sitting; the chain T001 to T102 is about 36 merges deep with four operator blocks, so the build takes about 40 sittings whatever the agent count, and the maintainerWaitSeconds that would reopen the merge decision exists only after about 89 of 102 tasks.
findings.change: In 12 12.9 add a merge-cadence rule (for example: a green pull request whose approval lines are present is merged in the next sitting, and a sitting happens at least once per working day) and allow consecutive dependent tasks of one chain written by one agent to ship as one pull request under the existing 'or is part of it' clause; move the trigger of the deferred row 'whether the maintainer's merge stays a manual checkpoint' from the first dora output to the first checkpoint whose phase had more than N pull requests waiting, counted by hand from GitHub until dora exists.
findings.cost: a rule and a changed trigger; no mechanism; the cadence is a commitment of the maintainer's time

findings.defect: The contracts surface (internal/cli/errors.go) and the checks surface (tools/ci/**) put an approval line with the maintainer's words on about two tasks in three, and 12 12.4 defines no approval that covers a class of change or a phase, so the maintainer is on the critical path of each such pull request twice.
findings.scenario: Phase 4: six romeu-cli tasks each append an error row; each pull request needs an Approval line for contracts typed from the maintainer's words; the maintainer is away two days; six green pull requests wait, and the plan's Ask-first forecast cannot stand in because tools/ci pr reads only the pull request body.
findings.change: Narrow contracts to internal/spec/versions.go once the RJ uniqueness check of L12-3 exists, so an appended error row is reviewed like any code; and in 12 12.4 define a checkpoint approval: a line of the same form recorded once in docs (for example docs/approvals.md or the plan's checkpoint) with the surface id and the phase, which tools/ci pr accepts for a pull request that names that checkpoint and touches no other surface.
findings.cost: one rule in 05 5.3, one clause in 12 12.4, a small extension of tools/ci pr (T005, not yet merged)

findings.defect: Error ids RJ-<exit><nn> are stable and asserted by tests, yet the spec allocates four of them and leaves the rest to whichever agent writes first, and no check in 10 10.2 asserts that RJ ids are unique.
findings.scenario: Two concurrent command tasks each add RJ-205 for a different error; both compile and pass; the second merges clean because the rows are on different lines; julieta and romeu now share one id for two errors and docs/reference/errors.md lists it twice.
findings.change: Add to 04 an allocation table (or per-command ranges: sync RJ-210 to RJ-219, approve RJ-220 to RJ-229, and so on, per exit code) that assigns every id named anywhere in 04 and 13 before the work is split, and add RJ-<n> to the id table of 10 10.2 so tools/ci sequences checks uniqueness and that every referenced id is defined.
findings.cost: a table in 04 and one row in the id table of 10 10.2; the check is a few lines in sequences (T004, not yet merged)

findings.defect: The tree shows cmd/romeu/main.go, cmd/julieta/main.go and internal/cli (dispatcher, error table) and no per-command package, so about 36 commands built by about 25 tasks register in one dispatcher table and one main.go each.
findings.scenario: Phase 4 runs sync, approve, status, doctor and adopt concurrently; every pull request edits cmd/romeu/main.go and the dispatcher's command list; each merge conflicts with the next, and tools/new command writes its stub into a file the spec never names.
findings.change: In 02 2.1 add one package per command under internal/cmd/romeu/<command> and internal/cmd/julieta/<command>, each registering through a file of its own that a generated command table (12 12.3, command definitions) assembles; say in 12 12.3 that tools/new command creates that package and its reference entry and touches no shared file.
findings.cost: two lines in the tree, one sentence in 12 12.3, a generator the command definitions row already implies

findings.defect: docs/lessons.md is one append-heavy file that the Boundaries ask every change to touch and tools/ci pr requires a Lessons section for, so any two concurrent pull requests that learned something conflict.
findings.scenario: Ten pull requests open in one phase, eight record a lesson; the seven that land after the first each need a rebase on a one-file conflict, and an agent resolving it by hand drops another's entry.
findings.change: Make lessons one file per lesson under docs/lessons/<ULID>-<slug>.md with a generated index docs/lessons/README.md, the shape ADRs already have (ADR 0001 rule 7); tools/new lesson writes the file, tools/ci lessons reads the directory; update 02 2.1 and the Boundaries.
findings.cost: a layout change before T006 creates the file; one generator row

findings.defect: Generated files with many writers (the error table's three consumers, the ledger's membership tables and schema, the ADR index) have no merge rule: the Never list forbids a hand edit and tools/ci generated fails a diff, but nothing says a conflict in a generated file is resolved by regeneration or requires generators to emit one member per line in a stable order.
findings.scenario: Two pull requests each add one error id; both regenerate docs/reference/errors.md; the second to land has a textual conflict in a generated file; the agent resolves it by hand (forbidden), generated fails one round later, and the pull request goes back for a rebase and a regenerate.
findings.change: Add to 12 12.3: every generator emits one record per line in a stable sort order so additive changes merge, a conflict in a generated file is resolved by checking out the base version and running go generate on the merged tree, and the table marks which generated files have more than one writing module; add a .gitattributes merge driver that does exactly that for the listed files, or state why not.
findings.cost: two sentences, one column in the generator table, an optional merge driver

findings.defect: Rule 7 requires contiguous ADR numbers and tools/new adr takes the next free one, so with about twenty records due in v1 (12 12.5: twenty open questions, five rounds of decisions, probe resolutions) concurrent decision records collide, and rule 9's cite-by-number multiplies the cost of a renumber.
findings.scenario: T028 and T027 both scaffold ADR 0009 in one week; the later one renames the file, rewrites the title line and every first mention in the spec; the plan avoids the problem by making T096 to T101 a six-deep serial chain of documentation pull requests at the end of the critical path.
findings.change: In ADR 0001 rule 7 keep uniqueness and drop contiguity for records (gaps allowed, checked unique by sequences), or add to 12 12.5 a reservation: each known future record (one per open question, one per round's decisions) gets its number in a committed table before it is written, and tools/new adr takes the reserved number for a named question; supersede by a new record since ADR 0001 is Accepted.
findings.cost: a superseding record or an amendment, one table, a small change to tools/new adr and sequences

findings.defect: The manifest is the one type both binaries marshal and decode, built by romeu-cli (phase 6) on one side and julieta-core (phase 5) on the other, and the spec names no Go package for it; 10 10.7 says which rows may be shared and not which seam uses which type.
findings.scenario: The julieta-core agent defines the manifest type under internal/mise or julieta's cmd; the romeu-cli agent defines another under internal/render; the hybrid handshake (T066) finds a field-name drift six phases after both were written.
findings.change: Name in 03 3.6 the shared package that owns the manifest type (for example internal/manifest, or a file of internal/spec), add it to the 'both' row of 10 10.7, and do the same for run-timings.v1 and probe-result.v1; state in 12 12.2 that a format's type lands with the first task on either side of its seam.
findings.cost: three package names and one sentence

findings.defect: Rule 13 fixes one committed file, e2e/scenarios/commands.yaml, that every host-facing command task appends to.
findings.scenario: T043, T045, T047, T048 and T050 each add lines for J2, J11, J7, J10 and J13; the file conflicts on every second merge of phase 4.

findings.defect: tools/ci is one tree for about 25 subcommands and their data, built by about 30 tasks, with no internal package layout in 02 2.1, and every generator is wired through the one admitted go:generate site tools/ci/generate.go (lint row; ADR 0007 rule 8).

findings.change: In 02 2.1 give tools/ci one package per step under tools/ci/internal/<step> and a dispatcher that discovers steps from a generated table or an init registration per package; let generate.go call a per-package list rather than hold every generator's wiring.
findings.cost: a tree entry and a sentence; the layout is cheaper now than after thirty tasks

findings.defect: The gate has no budget: all runs four lint targets, the race run, e2e on four runners, hybrid and container e2e, and mutate on every tools/ci pull request, and the fallback when the Actions quota runs out is the maintainer's own two machines, the same singleton as every operator block.

findings.change: State a target duration for fast and all in 10 10.2 next to the step table, say which steps run on Linux only to spare the macOS legs, and record a per-pull-request runner budget as a deferred decision with its trigger if a number cannot be set yet.
findings.cost: two numbers or one deferred row

findings.defect: A task is done when all passes on its branch, and 12 12.9 gates commits as the merge, but nothing says who re-runs all after a rebase, whether a merge queue exists, or who owns a date-dependent step (govulncheck, 10 10.2) that turns every open pull request red at once.

findings.change: Add to 10 10.8 that a pull request is re-gated by CI on the merge result (GitHub's merge queue or an equivalent rule) and that a govulncheck finding on main is one pull request owned by whoever first sees it, not a fix in every open branch.
findings.cost: two sentences and possibly a repository setting

postmortem: It is some months after v1.0.0. The product works on the maintainer's two machines and nobody else uses it, because by the time it shipped the maintainer had spent the year merging. (1) The build was one person wide: every merge waited for the maintainer by working agreement (12 12.9, index: Deferred decisions), every pull request on the contracts or checks surface needed the maintainer's words (05 5.3, 12 12.4), v1 had no stacks (12 12.9, ADR 0002); a dependency edge cost one sitting and the longest chain was about 36 edges with four operator blocks; tools/ci dora (12 12.10, ADR 0004) landed in phase 8 and the merge decision it was meant to reopen fired after the build it would have sped up. (2) Every command pull request touched the same files: internal/cli/errors.go (04 4.1, 05 5.3), the dispatcher with no per-command package (02 2.1), e2e/scenarios/commands.yaml (ADR 0001 rule 13) and docs/lessons.md (12 12.7); two tasks shipped the same RJ id because the spec allocated four and no check asserted uniqueness (10 10.2 sequences). (3) Generated files were the merge conflict: after the ledger landed (13 13.2, 12 12.3) every added command, error id, catalog key, invariant or probe regenerated the same tables and tools/ci generated refused the pull request that had not; the rule 'resolve by regeneration' was never written and agents resolved by hand. (4) The ADRs were a queue: about twenty records (12 12.5), contiguous numbers (ADR 0001 rule 7), citations by number (rule 9), an approval each (rule 8); the scaffold gave two agents the same number and the plan made six documentation tasks a serial chain at the end. (5) Block A was a cliff and the fake sbx a wall: 54 tasks waited on one two-host sitting (11 11.1, 12 12.2); the fake replayed only recorded shapes (10 10.3), the spec never listed them, A4 lacked the non-interactive exec form, A3 asked for product code that did not exist (11 opening); a render byte change moved A5's hash (03 3.3, 11 11.4) and both hosts sat again. (6) A11 said yes, barely, and had no written no branch (06 6.1, Q7). (7) The build order was a chain the plan had to disobey (12 12.2, plan question 3 unanswered). (8) The contracts were nowhere: the manifest (03 3.6) had no named package and 10 10.7 named no seam type; two agents wrote two types and the handshake caught it six phases later. (9) The gate ate the Actions quota with no budget (10 10.1, 10 10.2) and its fallback was the maintainer's laptops. (10) The quiet one: we measured five delivery metrics and never the count of maintainer utterances a pull request needs; the spec put a person at every joint of a machine built to remove people from the joints (index: Principles) and called it a working agreement.
lens_critique: This lens scores success as a short critical path, disjoint file sets and mechanical merges, and for this product that is only half right. The product's value is the security model (05) and the determinism principle (index), and several things that lengthen the path are the point: an ask-first surface is supposed to make a person look; a reviewed denylist, a probe on a real host and a maintainer merge are controls, not waste. The lens also over-values width: with one maintainer as the reviewer, a wider graph produces more green pull requests waiting, and the honest optimization is fewer, well-ordered sittings, not more agents. And it under-values the cost the spec does price, correctness of each piece: a chain of singletons through egress, render and gate also means one agent holds the whole gate 2 contract in its head, which has caught more bugs than it has cost days. The right reading of this lens for this product is: shorten the path where a person adds no judgment (id allocation, lessons files, generated-file merges, registries), and leave the person where the judgment is.
missing_viewpoint: The onboarding contributor who is not the maintainer and not an agent: a human second pair of hands who clones the repository, enables the hook, cannot pass the forbidden-names gate until the default branch is fetched, needs sbx on a Mac to run anything host-facing, and has to earn an approval line for almost every change. L10 (the second adopter) uses the product, L3 maintains it later, L14 is on duty; nobody in the set is the first outside contributor on day one, whose friction the delivery practices (12 12.9, ADR 0003 collective ownership) promise to serve and no page tests.
